newsitem.title: CHINA: HK may need new container port early next century.
newsitem.headline: HK may need new container port early next century.

text.p: Hong Kong will require a new container port early in the next century but actual construction of the port will depend on demand, Deputy Secretary for Economic Services Richard Yuen said on Friday.

The government has completed the preparatory work to build a new container port on the northern part of the territory's Lantau Island, including container terminals 10 to 13 (CT10-CT13), Yuen told a news briefing.
"Our current forecast is that the first terminal, Container Terminal 10, will be required in the early years of 2000, probably soon after the completion of the CT9 in 2002," he said.
Yuan said the project was aimed at taking advantage of the infrastructure and the road links built for the new airport at Chek Lap Kok off Lantau Island.
"The actual construction of Lantau Port will depend on demand and the actual growth rate of container throughput in Hong Kong," he added.
The government predicted Hong Kong's container throughput to grow by 8.5 percent a year. In 1996 the territory handled a total of 13.5 million TEUs (20-foot equivalent units).

"It is entirely possible as long as China's economy continues to growth in a modest way," Yuen said. "What it means is that we will need to add an additional one million TEU handling capacity to our port each year," he said.
About 9.0 million TEUs was handled by the eight container terminals in Hong Kong's Kwai Chung port last year and the balance was handled by river trade and mid-stream operations.
Construction of CT9 will begin early next year and expected to come in operation in May 1999. "We are finalising the land grant conditions with the developers for CT9," Yuen said.
CT9 will add 2.6 million TEU handling capacity to the Kwai Chung port when fully completed in 2002.
